claims.statement: Bounded base instruction form is or.b32 d, a, b;.

evidence.quotation:
or.type d, a, b;

.type = { .pred, .b16, .b32, .b64 };
In PTX, the fundamental types reflect the native data types supported by the target architectures. A fundamental type specifies both a basic type and a size.

claims.statement: Execution semantics in this unit are bitwise OR on 32-bit values: d <- a | b.

evidence.quotation: d = a | b;

The size of the operands must match, but not necessarily the type.
Allowed types include predicate registers.
Introduced in PTX ISA version 1.0.
Supported on all target architectures.
Bits (untyped) .b8, .b16, .b32, .b64, .b128

Most instructions have one or more type specifiers, needed to fully specify instruction behavior.
Operand types and sizes are checked against instruction types for compatibility.
Two fundamental types are compatible if they have the same basic type and are the same size. Signed and unsigned integer types are compatible if they have the same size. The bit-size type is compatible with any fundamental type having the same size.

claims.statement: Operand order is d then a then b; d is destination, a and b are sources, from PTX section 9.2 and family instruction form.

evidence.quotation:
or.type d, a, b;

.type = { .pred, .b16, .b32, .b64 };

claims.statement: Guarded execution follows '@p' / '@!p' syntax and false guard means instruction does nothing.

evidence.quotation: For some instructions the destination operand is optional. A bit bucket operand denoted with an underscore (_) may be used in place of a destination register.

All instructions have an optional guard predicate which controls conditional execution of the instruction. The syntax to specify conditional execution is to prefix an instruction with @{!}p, where p is a predicate variable, optionally negated.
All PTX instructions may be predicated. In the following descriptions, the optional guard predicate is omitted from the syntax.

@{!}p    instruction;
Execute an instruction or instruction block for threads that have the guard predicate True. Threads with a False guard predicate do nothing.
